question: Before a patient even gets to the hospital, what usually has the biggest impact on how they view their sickness?
explanation: You've got this! A person's culture and background shape how they feel symptoms and when they decide it's time to see a doctor. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is just treating the physical disease in a patient often not enough in community health?

options.A: Patients ignore their social and living realities
options.B: Hospitals lack sufficient beds for prolonged stays
options.C: Medications work independently of the environment
options.D: Social networks dictate post-discharge recovery success

explanation: Think about it like this: patients go back home to their families and communities. Their support system at home plays a huge role in whether they actually get better and stay better! [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h1)

question: According to family systems theory, how does illness in one family member affect the rest of the household?

options.A: Only the sick individual requires direct nursing care
options.B: Nuclear families experience less stress than extended ones
options.C: Financial stability prevents all forms of acute disease
options.D: A change in one member affects the whole family

explanation: Spot on! Families are connected like a web. When one person is going through an illness, the whole household feels the ripple effect. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h2)

question: A patient with high blood pressure won't change their diet because the whole family cooks and eats together. As a nurse, what should you do?

options.A: Advise the patient to cook separate meals alone every day
options.B: Involve the family members who prepare meals in dietary education
options.C: Report the family to the hospital management board
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately due to non-compliance

explanation: Great nursing judgment! Since the whole family shares meals, teaching the people who actually cook makes it much easier for the patient to stick to their new diet. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which type of family setup usually gives you the largest network of people to help share daily tasks and support?
explanation: Exactly! Living with or close to grandparents, aunts, uncles, and cousins means more hands on deck for caregiving and support. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is one of the biggest challenges a single-parent household often faces when a child falls chronically ill?

options.A: Automatic rejection by community health centers
options.B: Limited financial resources and time for caregiving
options.D: Complete lack of cultural health beliefs

explanation: It's tough! A single parent has to juggle earning money and providing care all by themselves, making long-term illnesses extra stressful. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h3)

question: What often happens when family members suddenly have to take on brand new roles because someone got sick?

options.D: Immediate financial surplus for the household

explanation: That's right. Taking on extra responsibilities without enough rest can quickly lead to physical and emotional burnout for family caregivers. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h4)

question: A teenager keeps missing school because they are busy nursing a sick parent at home. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advise the family to abandon all medical treatments
options.B: Connect the family with home-based care or community support services
options.C: Admit the teenager to the ward as a patient
options.D: Scold the teenager for missing important lectures

explanation: Wonderful approach! Linking them to outside help takes the heavy burden off the child so they can go back to school and be a kid again. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which tool does a nurse use to map out a family tree and track inherited health conditions across generations?
explanation: You got it! A genogram is essentially a detailed family medical tree that helps us spot hereditary health patterns easily. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is it so important for nurses to create care plans together with the family instead of just dictating them?

options.A: Hospital regulations forbid nurses from making independent decisions
options.B: Collaborative plans are more realistic and acceptable to the household
options.C: Families prefer writing medical prescriptions themselves
options.D: It eliminates the need for any follow-up visits

explanation: Spot on! When families help build the plan, it fits better into their daily routine and budget, making them much more likely to follow it. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the main job of a public health nurse out in the community?

options.B: Replacing traditional leaders in local governance
options.C: Bridging institutional health care and local community resources
options.D: Managing intensive care units in tertiary hospitals exclusively

explanation: Well done! Public health nurses act as a vital bridge, bringing hospital knowledge and community support together to keep people healthy where they live. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why is it super helpful for nurses to work hand-in-hand with local groups like religious organizations?

options.B: They can provide direct funding for hospital equipment
options.C: They hold significant influence over health behaviors and beliefs
options.D: They replace the need for professional nursing training

explanation: Exactly! Religious and community leaders are trusted by the people, so teaming up with them helps health messages stick and gain community trust. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h6)
